text:
Donald Trump won't be happy after CNN aired a montage of the 39 times he's promised the Iran war is nearing the end.

The conflict began on February 28 when the US and Israel launched airstrikes on the Middle Eastern country. In the months that have followed, President Trump has made multiple claims the U.S. has won the war and that peace deal negotiations are underway with Iran.

Despite Trump's previous claims, the conflict has continued. On Thursday Trump once again claimed the US has "ended the war in Iran" and said a "great settlement" has been reached. CNN host Anderson Cooper questioned Trump's latest claims as he hosted his show on June 11. It comes just days after a lip reader revealed Trump's desperate 8-word plea as he was brutally booed at the New York Knicks game.

Fans slam Jerry Seinfeld's 'vile' three-word response to Knicks fan's question after game

Fox News turns on Donald Trump as the network refuses to listen to his plea

"Today makes 39 times that he has said something like that," Anderson said as he aired a montage of all of the times Trump has claimed to have ended the war. Viewers praised Anderson for the segment on X.

"Just about as many times as he’s said, “the economy is great”, “gas prices will come down fast”, “we have the smartest people “. I mean, take your pick. He’s an idiot and I approve this message!" one CNN fan said. Another posted, "LOL 39 times. what a record for someone who boast as a negotiator. looks like he is a failure in everything. Get a move on fatso. Impeachment is incoming."

The first video in the CNN montage was from March 23. In the clip, Trump claimed to have "major points of agreement" with Iran before insisting "they wanna make a deal."

He continued, "We are very willing to make a deal."

A day later, Trump spoke to reporters at the White House and completely contradicted himself. He said, "Well, I think we're going to end it," but admitted, "I can't tell you for sure."

He later claimed during the same press conference, "They want to make a deal so badly. You have no idea how badly they want to make a deal."

It wasn't going to be the last time Trump has claimed Iran wants to make a deal to end the war. Speaking on March 25, the 79-year-old said, "They want to make a deal so badly."

Trump spoke with reporters while on board Air Force One on March 29. During the chat, he insisted, "I do see a deal in Iran."

By April 6, Trump subtly admitted he hadn't yet secured a deal in Iran despite claiming to have done so already. "We are very close to a deal," he told reporters.

Trump sat down for an interview with Fox News on April 15. During it, the president said, "I think it's close. I mean, I view it as very close to home."

He echoed these comments a day later. Trump spoke with reporters outside the White House on April 16 and claimed, "It's looking very good that we're going to make a deal with Iran." He also claimed it was "going to be a good deal."

"This process should go very quickly," Trump promised on April 17. By May 19, however, a deal still hadn't been made.

Trump repeated his promises, though, telling reporters, "We're going to end that war very quickly." He continued, "They wanna make a deal so badly."

Later that same day, he suggested, "We think we're close to a deal. And that's okay."

Trump spoke with reporters before boarding Air Force One on Monday, June 8, and admitted a deal is still yet to be reached. "We're in the final throes of what will be a very, very good deal."
